note: Authored practice pack for s19 (SQL + Databases). Short keys: s=sectionId, t=type, d=difficulty, i=importance, q=question, a=answer, x=explanation.

items.q: Relational database ko 'relational' kya banata hai, sirf rows aur columns se aage jaake?
items.a: Tables key relationships par organize hote hain: primary key ek row ki identity deta hai aur foreign key doosri table ki row ko point karta hai, isliye ek fact duplicate karne ke bajaye reference kiya jata hai.

items.q: Primary key me kaun si do properties laazmi hain aur kyun?
items.a: UNIQUE aur NOT NULL. Har row ko exactly ek identity chahiye, warna UPDATE ya join kisi ek specific row ko reliably target nahi kar sakta.
items.x: Identity ke bina row address nahi hoti.

items.q: Foreign key database level par kya enforce karta hai?
items.a: Referential integrity: child row ka value parent table me maujood ho (ya NULL ho), aur parent par DELETE/UPDATE hone par ON DELETE / ON UPDATE rule decide karta hai ki child ka kya hoga.
items.x: Orphan rows rokna foreign key ka kaam hai.

items.q: WHERE aur HAVING me asli farq kya hai?
items.a: WHERE rows par GROUP BY se pehle filter karta hai; HAVING aggregate ban jaane ke baad group level par filter karta hai, isliye COUNT(*)/SUM jaise conditions sirf HAVING me likhi ja sakti hain.

items.q: GROUP BY rows ke saath asli me kya karta hai?
items.a: Rows ko grouping key ke hisaab se buckets me daalta hai. Iske baad SELECT me sirf grouping key ya aggregate expressions aa sakte hain, kyunki har bucket me baaki columns ki kai values hoti hain.

items.q: ORDER BY kis baat ki guarantee deta hai aur kya guarantee nahi deta?
items.a: Sirf result ka order guarantee karta hai. Bina ORDER BY ke row order koi contract nahi hai, aur LIMIT ke saath order na dene par har run me different rows aa sakti hain.
items.x: Order tabhi hai jab likha ho.

items.q: Index read ko fast kaise karta hai aur uska kharcha kya hai?
items.a: Index ek sorted B-tree jaisa structure rakhta hai, isliye engine poora table scan karne ke bajaye seedha locate karta hai. Kharcha: har INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE par index bhi maintain karna padta hai aur disk space lagta hai.

items.q: 3NF normalisation kis concrete problem ko hatata hai?
items.a: Transitive dependency: ek non-key column ka doosre non-key column par depend karna. Isse ek hi fact kai jagah store hota hai aur update anomaly aata hai (ek jagah badla, doosri jagah purana).

items.q: Denormalization jaan-boojh kar kab karni chahiye?
items.a: Jab read path hi bottleneck ho aur join cost measurement me dikh rahi ho — reporting tables, counters ya materialized summaries me. Trade-off: read fast, par duplication aur consistency ki zimmedari app par.

items.q: ACID ke chaar letters exactly kya guarantee karte hain?
items.a: Atomicity: sab ya kuch nahi. Consistency: constraints nahi tootenge. Isolation: concurrent transactions ek doosre ka aadha-adhoora kaam nahi dekhengi. Durability: commit ke baad crash par bhi data bacha rahega.
items.x: Interview me chaaron ka matlab bolo.

items.q: ROLLBACK kis kaam ka hai aur COMMIT uske baad kya badalta hai?
items.a: ROLLBACK current transaction ke uncommitted changes undo karta hai (constraints bhi end me check hote hain). COMMIT ke baad changes durable ho jaate hain aur us transaction ko ROLLBACK se undo nahi kiya ja sakta.

items.q: View aur table me fundamental farq kya hai?
items.a: View ek saved query hai jo har reference par evaluate hota hai aur apna data store nahi karta (materialized view exception hai). Isliye view permissions aur query simplification ke liye use hota hai, storage ke liye nahi.

items.q: CTE aur subquery me kab kaunsa choose karoge?
items.a: CTE tab jab query ko readable steps me todna ho, ek hi result ko multiple baar reference karna ho, ya recursion chahiye. Subquery tab jab ek chhota single-use filter ya scalar value chahiye.

items.q: Window function GROUP BY se fundamentally kaise alag hai?
items.a: GROUP BY rows ko collapse kar deta hai (ek group = ek output row). Window function har row ko result me rakhta hai aur uske saath partition/order ke hisaab se running ya comparative value deta hai.

items.q: ROW_NUMBER, RANK aur DENSE_RANK me tie par kya farq padta hai?
items.a: ROW_NUMBER tie me bhi unique number deta hai (1,2,3). RANK ties ko same rank deta hai aur gap chhodta hai (1,1,3). DENSE_RANK same rank deta hai bina gap (1,1,2).
items.x: Gap hai ya nahi, bas yahi farq hai.

items.q: NULL ke saath '= NULL' kyun kabhi true nahi hota?
items.a: NULL ka matlab unknown hai, aur unknown ke saath koi bhi comparison NULL return karta hai (tritvalued logic), jo WHERE me true nahi mana jata. Isliye IS NULL / IS NOT NULL likhna padta hai.

items.q: Self join kis situation me majboori ban jaata hai?
items.a: Jab ek hi table ki row ko usi table ki doosri row se compare karna ho — employee ka manager, product ka replacement, ya consecutive events. Do aliases ke bina ek table ko do roles nahi diye ja sakte.

items.q: LEFT JOIN ka output INNER JOIN se kaise alag padhta hai?
items.a: LEFT JOIN left table ki saari rows rakhta hai aur match na hone par right side NULL se bhar deta hai. INNER JOIN sirf match hui rows deta hai, isliye count LEFT JOIN me zyada aa sakta hai.
items.x: Match na mile to NULL bharo.

items.q: Cross join aur normal join me kya farq hai, aur cross join galti se kab ban jata hai?
items.a: Cross join bina condition ke Cartesian product deta hai (m × n rows). Galti se ye tab banta hai jab ON condition bhoole ya aisi join likhi jaaye jisme dono tables me koi related column hi na ho.

items.q: Execution plan kis sawaal ka jawab deta hai?
items.a: Planner ne query chalane ka kya tarika chuna: kaun se scan, kis index se, kis join algorithm (nested loop, hash, merge) se, aur kahan sort/spill ho raha hai — yahi slow query ki asli wajah batata hai.
items.x: EXPLAIN andaza nahi, evidence deta hai.

items.q: 'Write a query to find the second highest salary' — approach kya hoga aur window function kyun prefer karoge?
items.a: DENSE_RANK use karo: SELECT * FROM (SELECT salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees) t WHERE r = 2. ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 ties par galat jawab deta hai.
items.x: Ties wala case hi asli test hai.

items.q: Duplicate rows ko dhoondhne aur safely delete karne ka SQL approach batao.
items.a: Pehle GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 se duplicate groups dikhao. Phir ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY id) ko subquery me le kar > 1 wale rows delete karo — aur delete se pehle wahi WHERE SELECT me chalao.
items.x: Group dikhao, rank lagao, phir delete.

items.q: Index kis case me query ko slow kar sakta hai?
items.a: Jab write-heavy table par bahut indexes hon (har write par sab update hote hain), jab column ki selectivity kam ho (gender jaisa), ya jab low-cardinality column par index ho aur planner use ignore kar de.

items.q: N+1 query problem kya hai aur ORM ke saath kaise pakadoge?
items.a: Ek list query ke baad har item ke liye alag query chalti hai (1 + N). Pakadne ke liye SQL logging on karo aur ek page load par query count dekho; fix eager loading (JOIN / select_related / include) ya batch fetch se hota hai.

items.q: COUNT(*) aur COUNT(column) me farq batao.
items.a: COUNT(*) saari rows ginta hai, NULL values wali rows bhi. COUNT(column) sirf non-NULL values ginta hai, isliye open questions ka hissa nikalne ke liye COUNT(col) vs COUNT(*) ka ratio kaafi useful hota hai.

items.q: LEFT JOIN ke baad WHERE right.id IS NULL ka matlab kya nikalta hai?
items.a: Woh left rows jinka koi match nahi mila — classic anti-join. Isi se 'customers jinhone kabhi order nahi kiya' jaisa sawal answer hota hai.

items.q: Transactions me deadlock kaise banta hai aur application level par kya karoge?
items.a: Do transactions opposite order me same rows lock karte hain, phir dono ek doosre ka lock wait karte hain. Fix: sab code me consistent lock/sort order rakho, transactions chhoti rakho, aur retry with backoff implement karo.

items.q: SQL injection se bachne ka correct tarika kya hai?
items.a: Parameterized queries / prepared statements use karo — values ko SQL string me concatenate mat karo. Jo query string banane ke liye f-string psst karta hai, wahi injection ka darwaza kholta hai.

items.q: Production me ek query 3 second se 30 second ho gayi — step by step kaise approach karoge?
items.a: Pehle EXPLAIN/EXPLAIN ANALYZE se plan dekho (seq scan, missing index, bad row estimate), tables ki size aur recent row growth dekho, phir index add karo ya query rewrite karo, aur change ke baad plan dobara verify karo. Blind index add karna guesswork hai.

items.q: Window function se running total kaise nikaloge?
items.a: SELECT date, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running FROM sales; — GROUP BY ke bina per-row output milta hai.
items.x: OVER + frame hi running total hai.

items.q: UNION aur UNION ALL me choice kaise karte hain?
items.a: UNION duplicate rows hata deta hai, isliye internally sort/hash lagta hai. UNION ALL sirf results jodta hai aur sasta hota hai — jab duplicates possible hi nahi (different tables ya disjoint filters) tab UNION ALL use karo.

items.q: CTE aur temp table me production me kab kaunsa choose karoge?
items.a: CTE tab jab logic ek query ke andar readable pipeline ho. Temp table tab jab same intermediate result ko kai queries me reuse karna ho, uspar index chahiye, ya query itni badi ho ki planner use samajh na paaye.

items.q: Upsert (insert-or-update) kaise likhoge aur race condition se kaise bachoge?
items.a: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET ... (Postgres/SQLite) use karo — SELECT karke phir INSERT karne me do requests ke beech race hoti hai. Unique constraint hi final truth hai.

items.q: Read replica lag hone par stale data se bachne ka approach kya hai?
items.a: Read-after-write ko replica par mat bhejo: recent writes wali request primary par chalao, ya sticky session rakho, ya write ke response me version/timestamp bhejo aur replica se min version maango.

items.q: Pagination me OFFSET high hone par query slow kyun hoti hai, aur keyset pagination kaise better hai?
items.a: OFFSET n wale page ke liye engine n rows scan karke phenkta hai. Keyset pagination WHERE (created_at, id) < (last_seen_ts, last_seen_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20 se index se seedha agla page padhta hai — cost page number se independent.

items.q: Clustered aur non-clustered index me farq interview me kaise explain karoge?
items.a: Clustered index hi data ka physical order decide karta hai (ek table me ek), isliye range scan sasta hota hai. Non-clustered index alag structure hai jisme pointer/key hota hai, aur lookup ke liye extra jump lagta hai.
items.x: Ek order set karta hai, doosra sirf map.

items.q: ACID ko product manager ki bhasha me 3 lines me kaise samjhaoge?
items.a: Ek transaction ya poora lagega ya bilkul nahi (atomicity), data ke rules kabhi tootenge nahi (consistency), do users ek saath kaam karte hain to ek doosre ka aadha kaam nahi dekhenge (isolation), aur ek baar 'saved' bole to crash ke baad bhi saved rahega (durability).
items.x: Business impact ki bhasha me bolo.

items.q: Stored procedure me business logic likhna kab sahi decision hota hai?
items.a: Tab jab logic data ke itne kareeb ho ki network round-trips bachane ho aur kai applications same invariant share karte hon. Downside: version control, testing aur deployment mushkil; isliye simple cases app layer me hi rakho.

items.q: employees table se har department ka average salary nikalo, sirf un departments ke liye jahan 3 se zyada employees hain.
items.a:
SELECT department, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
ORDER BY avg_salary DESC;
items.x: Group ke baad wala filter HAVING me jata hai.

items.q: students table se top 3 marks wale students ke naam nikalo, aur ties me sab dikhein.
items.a:
SELECT name, marks
FROM (SELECT name, marks, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY marks DESC) AS r FROM students) t
WHERE r <= 3
ORDER BY marks DESC, name;
items.x: DENSE_RANK ties ko gap deta hai, LIMIT nahi.

items.q: customers aur sales join karke har customer ka total order value nikalo — jo customer ne kabhi order nahi kiya woh bhi 0 ke saath dikhe.
items.a:
SELECT c.id, c.name, COALESCE(SUM(s.amount), 0) AS total
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total DESC;
items.x: LEFT JOIN + COALESCE se missing rows 0 ban jaati hain.

items.q: sales table se monthly revenue nikalo (YYYY-MM format me).
items.a:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM sales
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
items.x: SQLite me strftime se date truncate hota hai.

items.q: Har department ka sabse zyada salary wala employee nikalo.
items.a:
SELECT department, name, salary
FROM (SELECT department, name, salary,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
      FROM employees) t
WHERE rn = 1;
items.x: PARTITION BY se per-group ek row milti hai.

items.q: students table me duplicate email wale records dhoondhne ke liye query likho.
items.a:
SELECT email, COUNT(*) AS copies
FROM students
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY copies DESC;

items.q: Un customers ki list nikalo jinhone pichhle 30 din me koi order nahi kiya.
items.a:
SELECT c.id, c.name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN sales s
  ON s.customer_id = c.id AND s.sale_date >= date('now', '-30 day')
WHERE s.id IS NULL;
items.x: Filter ON me rakho, warna LEFT JOIN inner ban jata hai.

items.q: sales table me date order me running total nikalo.
items.a:
SELECT sale_date, amount,
       SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date, id
                         ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_total
FROM sales
ORDER BY sale_date, id;
items.x: Frame clause running total ko explicit banata hai.

items.q: expenses table me har category ka percentage share nikalo total ka.
items.a:
SELECT category,
       SUM(amount) AS total,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(amount) / (SELECT SUM(amount) FROM expenses), 2) AS pct
FROM expenses
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY total DESC;
items.x: 100.0 likhna zaroori hai warna integer division 0 dega.

items.q: employees me self join se har employee ke saath uska manager ka naam dikhao.
items.a:
SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager
FROM employees e
LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id
ORDER BY e.name;
items.x: Same table do aliases ke saath.

items.q: sales me month-over-month growth percentage nikalo (LAG ke saath).
items.a:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS revenue
  FROM sales GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month))
             / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS growth_pct
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month;
items.x: LAG pichhli row ki value laata hai.

items.q: students ke marks ko CASE expression se grade (A/B/C/Fail) me convert karo.
items.a:
SELECT name, marks,
       CASE WHEN marks >= 90 THEN 'A'
            WHEN marks >= 75 THEN 'B'
            WHEN marks >= 40 THEN 'C'
            ELSE 'Fail' END AS grade
FROM students
ORDER BY marks DESC;
items.x: CASE me order matter karta hai — bada threshold pehle.

items.q: Har region ke top 2 customers nikaalo (revenue ke hisaab se).
items.a:
SELECT region, name, revenue
FROM (SELECT c.region, c.name, SUM(s.amount) AS revenue,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.region ORDER BY SUM(s.amount) DESC) AS rn
      FROM customers c JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id
      GROUP BY c.id, c.region, c.name) t
WHERE rn <= 2
ORDER BY region, revenue DESC;
items.x: Window function aggregate ke upar bhi lag sakta hai.

items.q: Har customer ka pehla order date aur amount nikalo.
items.a:
SELECT customer_id, sale_date AS first_order, amount
FROM (SELECT customer_id, sale_date, amount,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY sale_date, id) AS rn
      FROM sales) t
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY customer_id;

items.q: customers table me kitne rows me email NULL hai?
items.x: NULL ke liye = nahi, IS NULL likhna hai.

items.q: Employees nikalo jinki salary 50000 se zyada hai par department HR nahi hai.
items.a:
SELECT name, department, salary
FROM employees
WHERE salary > 50000 AND department <> 'HR'
ORDER BY salary DESC;
items.x: NOT + AND ko parenthesise karke likhna habit banao.

items.q: chat_logs me sabse busy hour nikalo (kitne messages us hour me).
items.a:
SELECT strftime('%H', created_at) AS hour, COUNT(*) AS messages
FROM chat_logs
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY messages DESC
LIMIT 1;
items.x: Timestamp ko hour me truncate karke group karo.

items.q: expenses ka 3-month moving average nikaalo.
items.a:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', spent_on) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total
  FROM expenses GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, total,
       ROUND(AVG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS ma3
FROM monthly ORDER BY month;
items.x: Frame 2 PRECEDING se rolling window banta hai.

items.q: students table ke median marks nikalo (SQL window function ke saath).
items.a:
SELECT AVG(marks) AS median
FROM (SELECT marks,
             ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY marks) AS rn,
             COUNT(*) OVER () AS n
      FROM students) t
WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2);
items.x: Even count par do middle rows ka average median deta hai.

items.q: sales me aise customers dhoondo jinka order total 10000 se zyada hai (aggregate filter).
items.a:
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS lifetime
FROM sales
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(amount) > 10000
ORDER BY lifetime DESC;

items.q: Bina ORDER BY ke LIMIT 10 laga hua query likhna production me kyun risky hai — interview me iska jawab kaise doge?
items.a: Risky: SELECT * FROM sales LIMIT 10; — row order guarantee nahi, isliye different runs me alag rows. Safe: SELECT * FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date DESC, id DESC LIMIT 10; — deterministic tie-breaker ke saath.

items.q: employees me manager_id 4 rows me NULL hai. SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(manager_id) FROM employees; dono columns kya dikhayenge?
items.a: COUNT(*) total rows (jaise 12) dikhayega, COUNT(manager_id) sirf non-NULL values (8) dikhayega — NULL kabhi count nahi hota.

items.q: SELECT department, name FROM employees GROUP BY department; — SQLite me ye kya dega?
items.a: SQLite ise chalne de sakta hai (bare column ko arbitrary row se pick karta hai), par result ka koi meaning nahi hota. Strict engines error dete hain. Sahi tarika: name ko aggregate (MAX/group_concat) me daalo ya GROUP BY me dept + name dono likho.

items.q: WHERE marks > 80 AND marks < 90 wali condition 100 students me se tab kya karegi jab marks me kuch NULL hon?
items.a: NULL wale students condition pass nahi karenge (comparison NULL deta hai, true nahi), isliye woh silently result se bahar ho jaayenge — chahiye to OR marks IS NULL add karo.
items.x: NULL silently filter ho jaata hai.

items.q: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id; — ye kya ginega, customers ya orders?
items.a: Orders ke rows ginega (har match ek row deta hai; bina order wale customer ke liye ek NULL row bhi ginti hai). Unique customers chahiye to COUNT(DISTINCT c.id) likho.
items.x: Join ke baad grain badal jata hai.

items.q: Do queries: (A) WHERE dept='HR' AND salary>50000, (B) WHERE salary>50000 AND dept='HR' — result same hoga?
items.a: Haan, AND commutative hai aur dono conditions row level par lagti hain, isliye output identical. Jo same nahi hota woh WHERE vs HAVING ka farq hai.
items.x: AND ka order result nahi badalta.

items.q: LEFT JOIN ke baad WHERE s.amount > 100 likhne par kaunsa join ban jata hai?
items.a: Practically INNER JOIN, kyunki bina match wali rows me s.amount NULL hota hai aur NULL > 100 true nahi hota — woh rows chhant jaati hain. Filter ON me rakho to LEFT behaviour bacha rahega.
items.x: WHERE ka filter LEFT ko inner bana deta hai.

items.q: SELECT name FROM students WHERE marks NOT IN (SELECT marks FROM students WHERE marks IS NULL); — output kya aayega?
items.a: Khaali result. NOT IN ke andar NULL aaya to poora condition NULL ban jata hai aur koi row pass nahi karti — NOT EXISTS ya IS NOT NULL wala filter chahiye.

items.q: SELECT 7/2, 7.0/2; — SQL me dono columns kya denge?
items.a: 7/2 integer division hai → 3. 7.0/2 me ek operand decimal hai → 3.5. Isliye percentage/average nikalte waqt 100.0 likhna padta hai.
items.x: Integer division silently truncate karta hai.

items.q: GROUP BY dept ke saath SELECT dept, SUM(salary) chala. SUM(NULL) wale group par kya hoga?
items.a: SUM NULL values ko ignore karta hai; agar group me sirf NULL salaries hain to SUM NULL dega (0 nahi). COALESCE(SUM(salary), 0) se display safe rakh sakte ho.
items.x: SUM khaali set par NULL deta hai.

items.q: ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1 kab galat jawab de sakta hai?
items.a: Jab top salary par tie ho: pehli row skip karke doosri tie wali row aayegi, jo 'second highest' nahi hai. DENSE_RANK wala approach isi wajah se correct hai.

items.q: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY sale_date) wali subquery WHERE rn = 1 de rahi hai. Agar ORDER BY me tie ho to output?
items.a: Tie par order arbitrary hota hai, isliye deterministic result ke liye ORDER BY sale_date, id likho — id tie-breaker ke bina same customer ke do orders me se koi bhi rn=1 ban sakta hai.

items.q: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM sales; aur SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM sales) t; me farq hai?
items.a: Result same aata hai, par pehla ek hi pass me distinct count karta hai aur chhota likha jata hai; doosra inner query ka poora result bana kar count karta hai — bade data par mehnga.

items.q: SELECT * FROM students WHERE name LIKE 'a%'; — kya match karega aur case sensitivity ka kya scene hai?
items.a: Sirf woh names jo 'a' se shuru hote hain (LIKE ASCII case-insensitive hai, isliye 'Ashu' bhi match karega). Bada dataset par leading wildcard '%a' index use nahi karne dega.
items.x: Prefix wildcard index ke saath chalta hai, suffix nahi.

items.q: UNION ke dono sides me column count same hai par data type different (INT aur TEXT) — kya hoga?
items.a: Engine types ko common type me coerce karega (TEXT), isliye sorting/comparison expected na ho — yahi bug ka source hota hai. UNION ALL ke saath bhi same coercion rule lagta hai.

items.q: Ek customer ke 5 orders hain. SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) FROM sales GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 5; — kitni rows aayengi?
items.a: Zero rows — condition strictly > hai, aur 5 > 5 false hai. >= 5 likhna padta hai. Off-by-one HAVING me sabse common interview trap hai.
items.x: > aur >= ka farq boundary par dikhta hai.

items.q: Bina WHERE ke DELETE FROM sales; (jab tak transaction me ho) aur TRUNCATE ka behaviour kaise alag hota hai?
items.a: DELETE row-by-row karta hai, triggers chalta hai, WHERE de sakte ho aur rollback ho sakta hai. TRUNCATE pages drop karta hai — tez, par triggers/logs bypass aur rollback karna mushkil/na-mumkin.

items.q: SELECT MAX(marks) - MIN(marks) FROM students; — ye kis cheez ka answer deta hai aur kya nahi?
items.a: Range (spread) deta hai, average ya median nahi. Outliers range ko chhupa sakte hain, isliye distribution samajhne ke liye median/percentile bhi dekhna chahiye.
items.x: Range outlier se distort hoti hai.

items.q: Ek query EXPLAIN me 'SCAN sales' dikha rahi hai jabki index bhi maujood hai. Sabse pehla check kya karoge?
items.a: Dekho ki WHERE/SELECT me expression index ko wrap to nahi kar raha — jaise WHERE strftime('%Y', sale_date) = '2026' ya WHERE amount + 0 > 100. Index use karne ke liye column ko bare rakho: sale_date >= '2026-01-01' AND sale_date < '2027-01-01'.
items.x: Function column par lagaya to index marr gaya.

items.q: Ye query error de rahi hai: SELECT department, name, AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department; — kya galat hai aur fix kya hai?
items.a: SELECT list me 'name' grouped ya aggregated nahi hai. Fix: GROUP BY department, name rakho (agar per-employee chahiye) ya name hata do / MAX(name) use karo (agar per-department chahiye).
items.x: Non-aggregated column GROUP BY me hona chahiye.

items.q: Ye query chal rahi hai par galat count de rahi hai: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id; — expected 40 customers, mila 260. Wajah?
items.a: Join ke baad grain sales ke level par chala gaya (har order ek row), isliye count orders ho gaya. Fix: COUNT(DISTINCT c.id), ya EXISTS/IN wali subquery use karo.
items.x: Join ke baad grain change ho jata hai.

items.q: Ye query khaali result de rahi hai: SELECT * FROM sales WHERE paid_date = NULL; — bina hisaab dekhe bug kya hai?
items.a: NULL ke saath = kabhi true nahi hota, isliye condition kisi row par match nahi karti. Fix: WHERE paid_date IS NULL (unpaid orders ke liye) ya IS NOT NULL (paid ke liye).

items.q: Anti-join likha tha par zero rows aa gayi: SELECT * FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE s.amount > 0 OR s.amount IS NULL; — intent 'no paid orders' tha. Bug pakdo.
items.a: OR s.amount IS NULL ne bina order wale customers ke saath woh customers bhi wapas le aaye jinke saare orders NULL amount wale hain, aur LEFT JOIN ke NULL rows condition ko true bana dete hain. Sahi: WHERE s.id IS NULL.
items.x: NULL ko condition me true mat banao.

items.q: Query: SELECT name marks FROM students; — kya error aayega aur kyun?
items.a: Syntax error (comma missing) — 'name marks' ko engine ek table alias samajhta hai. Fix: SELECT name, marks FROM students;. Comma bhoole to error, par kabhi-kabhi silently galat alias ban jaata hai.
items.x: Ruki hui comma hi 90% syntax errors hain.

items.q: Ye query 0 deti hai: SELECT 100 * SUM(paid) / COUNT(*) FROM orders; jabki paid 60 of 100 hai. Expected 60. Fix?
items.a: Integer division: SUM(paid) bhi int hai aur COUNT(*) bhi, isliye decimal part truncate ho jata hai. Fix: 100.0 * SUM(paid) / COUNT(*).

items.q: Duplicate delete script ne saare copies uda diye: DELETE FROM students WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) rn FROM students) t WHERE rn > 1); — sab kis case me delete honge?
items.a: Agar email NULL hai to PARTITION BY NULL sab NULL-emails ko ek group me daal deta hai aur rn > 1 wale sab delete — baad me sirf ek bachta hai. Fix: WHERE email IS NOT NULL AND ... , aur delete se pehle wahi SELECT dry-run karo.
items.x: NULL partition sabko ek bucket banata hai.

items.q: Ye query slow hai: WHERE date(sale_date) = '2026-09-24'. Index sale_date par hai. Kya change karoge?
items.a: date() ne column ko wrap kar diya, isliye index use nahi hota. Fix: WHERE sale_date >= '2026-09-24' AND sale_date < '2026-09-25' — sargable range condition index use karne deti hai.

items.q: Order by ke bina pagination de rahi hai different results: SELECT * FROM sales LIMIT 20 OFFSET 40; — fix kya hai?
items.a: ORDER BY missing hai, isliye page boundaries non-deterministic hain (rows repeat/skip ho sakti hain). Fix: ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC — aur long term me keyset pagination use karo.
items.x: Pagination ka contract order par tika hai.

items.q: CTE wali query recursive ban gayi aur end nahi ho rahi (infinite loop). Kya check karoge?
items.a: Recursive CTE me termination condition missing hai — join me aisa column match ho raha hai jo khud ko dobara produce karta hai, ya cycle check nahi hai. Fix: base case strictly chhota karo aur cycle guard (visited path) rakho.
items.x: Recursion ka exit base case hi hota hai.

items.q: Query 'department' column not found de rahi hai jabki employees table me woh column hai. Sabse common wajah?
items.a: Join me dono tables me same naam wala column hai aur engine doosri table me dhoondh raha hai — qualify karo: SELECT e.department FROM employees e;. Alias se qualify karna habit banao.

items.q: Ye query expected 5 departments deti hai par 4 deti hai: SELECT department FROM employees GROUP BY department; — 100 employees me 6 rows me department NULL hai. Wajah?
items.a: GROUP BY NULL ko bhi ek group maanta hai, isliye 5th group NULL hai — aur agar reporting code NULL drop karta ho to 4 dikhta hai. WHERE department IS NOT NULL se intent clear karo.
items.x: NULL ek group ban jaata hai.

items.q: upsert ke baad duplicate rows aa gayi: pehle SELECT karke check kiya tha ki row nahi hai, phir INSERT. Concurrent requests par kya galat hua?
items.a: Check-then-insert race hai — dono requests ne SELECT me 'nahi hai' dekha aur dono ne INSERT kar diya. Fix: UNIQUE constraint + INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (ya DO NOTHING).

items.q: Deadlock error aata hai sirf tab jab do workers ek saath chalte hain. Transaction code me kya fix karoge?
items.a: Locks ka order unify karo: dono transactions same order me tables/rows touch karein (jaise hamesha accounts ko id ASC me). Saath me transaction ko chhota karo aur deadlock par bounded retry add karo.
items.x: Consistent lock ordering deadlock todta hai.

items.q: Ye filter data gum kar raha hai: WHERE status IN ('paid', 'PENDING ') — 12 pending orders missing hain. Bug?
items.a: Trailing space — 'PENDING ' vs 'PENDING' match nahi karta. Fix: app me value trim karke store karo (aur upload ke waqt TRIM lagao), warna stored data hi inconsistent hai.

items.q: Window function wali query duplicate rows de rahi hai: SELECT order_id, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) FROM sales; — user ko per-customer ek total chahiye tha. Bug?
items.a: Window function har input row ko output deta hai, isliye har order ke saath customer total repeat hota hai. Per-customer ek row chahiye to GROUP BY customer_id, ya window ke saath DISTINCT/deduped subquery.

items.q: Date comparison galat hai: WHERE sale_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30' — 30 September ke baad ke records missing hain. Kya hua?
items.a: Agar sale_date me time bhi hai to '2026-09-30 10:00' > '2026-09-30' hota hai aur between se bahar reh jaata hai. Fix: >= start AND < next_day_start use karo.
items.x: BETWEEN inclusive hai, par time usse tod deta hai.

items.q: Ye statement kya karega: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Ashu'); — do columns list, ek value?
items.a: Column list me do columns hain par values ek — engine error dega (ya kuch engines missing value par NULL/default bhar dete hain). Hamesha column list aur values ka count match karo.

items.q: Index hone ke baad bhi query slow hai: WHERE lower(email) = 'a@x.com' — fix kya hai?
items.a: lower(email) index ko bypass karta hai. Fix options: expression index (CREATE INDEX ... ON users (lower(email))), ya email ko normalize karke store karo (case-insensitive collation / CITEXT jaisa).

items.q: HAVING order by ke saath error de raha hai: SELECT dept, SUM(salary) s FROM employees GROUP BY dept HAVING s > 100000; — kab ye fail hoga?
items.a: Jab engine ko alias HAVING me allowed na ho (kai engines sirf ORDER BY me alias allow karte hain). Fix: HAVING SUM(salary) > 100000 likho — portable hai aur intent wahi.
items.x: Alias sab jagah allowed nahi hota.

items.q: Migration ke baad app crash kar rahi hai: NOT NULL column add kiya but purane rows me NULL hai. Fix approach?
items.a: ALTER TABLE par NOT NULL tabhi lagega jab default ho ya pehle backfill ho. Safe migration: column nullable add → batch backfill → NOT NULL + DEFAULT → phir constraint lagao (aur ek transaction per step).

items.q: Aapka retention query galat cohort de raha hai: connected rows ko date equality se join kar raha hai jabki signup timestamp me time hai. Fix?
items.a: Timestamps ko poore day/week buckets me normalize karo (date(created_at), strftime('%Y-%W', ...)), phir usi bucket par cohort join karo. Time component equality ko todta hai.

items.q: Real-world: ek e-commerce dashboard ka 'Monthly Active Buyers' number reviewers doubt kar rahe hain. Aap kaise verify karoge?
items.a: Definition lock karo (unique customers with at least one paid order in the month), phir query: SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.paid_at) m, COUNT(DISTINCT o.customer_id) FROM orders o WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY m — aur refunded/cancelled ko explicitly exclude karke count ko raw table ke distinct count se cross-check karo.

items.q: Real-world: customer churn define karke query likhni hai — 60 din se koi paid order nahi.
items.a: WITH last_order AS (SELECT customer_id, MAX(paid_at) AS last_paid FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT l.customer_id, l.last_paid FROM last_order l WHERE l.last_paid < datetime('now', '-60 day'); — aur active-but-no-order customers ko alag bucket me dikhao.

items.q: Real-world: signup funnel (visit → signup → first order) drop-off percentage nikaalna hai.
items.a: SELECT step, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) users, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) / MAX(COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)) OVER (), 2) pct FROM events WHERE step IN ('visit','signup','first_order') GROUP BY step ORDER BY CASE step WHEN 'visit' THEN 1 WHEN 'signup' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END;
items.x: Funnel = ordered steps + percentage of top.

items.q: Real-world: duplicate customer records merge karne hain (same email, different ids). Safe approach?
items.a: 1) SELECT email, COUNT(*), MIN(id) keep_id, group_concat(id) ids FROM customers GROUP BY lower(email) HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; 2) child rows (orders) ko keep_id par UPDATE karo; 3) duplicate ids delete karo — aur ye sab ek transaction me, pehle backup/export ke saath.

items.q: Real-world: ek analyst ki query 20M rows wali sales table par 90 second leti hai. Rewrite plan batao.
items.a: Pehle EXPLAIN ANALYZE se actual time aur row counts dekho. Phir: query ko sargable banao (column par function hatao), zaroori composite index banao (customer_id, sale_date), pre-aggregate ko summary table/materialized view me daalo, aur reporting ke liye partition pruning wala date filter mandatory karo.

items.q: Real-world: 'top 10 products by revenue last quarter, refunds excluded' — query likhne se pehle kya clarify karoge?
items.a: Refund handling (net revenue ya gross minus refunds?), quarter definition (calendar ya fiscal), product grain (SKU ya category), aur time zone. Phir query me in decisions ko comments me likho: SELECT p.name, SUM(o.amount) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON ... JOIN products p ON ... WHERE o.paid_at >= :q_start AND o.paid_at < :q_end AND o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY p.id, p.name ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 10;
items.x: Definition clarify karna query se pehle aata hai.

items.q: Real-world: production me ek reporting query ne primary database slow kar diya. Turant aur permanent fix?
items.a: Turant: query cancel/limit karo ya read replica par bhejo, aur long-running reports ko rate limit. Permanent: read replica + nightly pre-aggregation table, indexes verify, aur reports ko statement timeout ke saath chalao.
items.x: Reporting ko OLTP se alag karo.

items.q: Real-world: A/B test results table se variant-wise conversion rate nikalna hai.
items.a: SELECT variant, COUNT(*) users, SUM(converted) conversions, ROUND(1.0 * SUM(converted) / COUNT(*), 4) AS cvr FROM experiment_assignments GROUP BY variant; — aur significance ke liye per-user level counts bhi rakho, sirf rate se nateeja na maano.
items.x: Rate ke saath sample size bhi dikhao.

items.q: Real-world: slowly changing dimension (customer plan change history) track karni hai. Schema kaise design karoge?
items.a: Effective-dated rows: customer_id, plan, valid_from, valid_to (ya is_current flag), aur overlap rokne ke liye UNIQUE (customer_id, valid_from) + check valid_to > valid_from. Query me point-in-time join: ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id AND s.at >= c.valid_from AND (c.valid_to IS NULL OR s.at < c.valid_to).

items.q: Real-world: daily active users (DAU) trend ke saath 7-day moving average chahiye.
items.a: WITH d AS (SELECT date(created_at) day, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) dau FROM events GROUP BY day) SELECT day, dau, ROUND(AVG(dau) OVER (ORDER BY day ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 1) dau_ma7 FROM d ORDER BY day;

items.q: Real-world: expenses ka month-wise budget vs actual variance report chahiye.
items.a: WITH actual AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', spent_on) m, SUM(amount) amt FROM expenses GROUP BY m) SELECT a.m, a.amt actual, b.planned budget, a.amt - b.planned variance, ROUND(100.0 * (a.amt - b.planned) / b.planned, 1) variance_pct FROM actual a LEFT JOIN budgets b ON b.month = a.m ORDER BY a.m;

items.q: Real-world: data quality audit — kis table me kitne NULL/duplicate/out-of-range values hain, ek query set me batao.
items.a: Har rule ke liye ek query: NULL audit (SELECT 'customers.email' col, COUNT(*) - COUNT(email) nulls FROM customers UNION ALL ...), duplicate audit (GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1), range audit (WHERE marks < 0 OR marks > 100). Phir results ko ek checks table me union karke report banao.

items.q: Real-world: 'customer lifetime value' (LTV) nikalna hai simple version me.
items.a: SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(s.id) orders, COALESCE(SUM(s.amount), 0) revenue, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(s.amount), 0) / NULLIF(COUNT(s.id), 0), 2) AS aov FROM customers c LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name ORDER BY revenue DESC;

items.q: Real-world: support team ke liye 'first response time' nikalna hai tickets table se.
items.a: SELECT ticket_id, MIN(created_at) opened, MIN(CASE WHEN actor = 'agent' THEN created_at END) first_agent_reply, ROUND((julianday(MIN(CASE WHEN actor='agent' THEN created_at END)) - julianday(MIN(created_at))) * 24 * 60, 1) AS minutes_to_first_reply FROM ticket_events GROUP BY ticket_id;
items.x: Conditional aggregate se pehla agent reply.

items.q: Real-world: cohort retention week-wise nikalni hai (signup week vs activity week).
items.a: WITH signup AS (SELECT user_id, strftime('%Y-%W', created_at) cohort FROM users), activity AS (SELECT DISTINCT user_id, strftime('%Y-%W', created_at) week FROM events) SELECT s.cohort, a.week, COUNT(DISTINCT s.user_id) users FROM signup s JOIN activity a USING (user_id) GROUP BY s.cohort, a.week ORDER BY s.cohort, a.week;
items.x: Week key dono tables me same format me banao.

items.q: Real-world: production data fix karna hai (wrong currency values) — safe rollout kaise karoge?
items.a: Transaction me: 1) affected rows count karo (SELECT ... WHERE currency IS NULL OR currency NOT IN ('INR','USD')), 2) ek idempotent UPDATE chalao with explicit WHERE, 3) same WHERE se count dobara verify karo, 4) commit karo aur count log karo; app code ko bhi default currency dena sikhayein.

items.q: Real-world: interviewer poochta hai tumhare project me SQL layer kitna load leta hai — kya measure karke bataoge?
items.a: Query latency p50/p95, queries per request, slow query log ke top offenders, aur index hit ratio. Number ke saath bolo: 'p95 40ms, 6 queries per request, sabse slow query top-N products hai jiska EXPLAIN seq scan dikhata tha'.

items.q: Real-world: ek 'orders by city' report me 12% orders 'unknown city' me ja rahe hain. Debug plan?
items.a: Data se shuru karo: SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY city ORDER BY 2 DESC; phir joins ke dono side dekho — NULL city, blank string, aur case/whitespace variants ('delhi' vs 'Delhi '). Fix: normalize on write (trim + case) aur mapping table se enrich karo.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare schema me foreign key lagayi thi — interviewer poochta hai kyun, ORM me to relation alag se define hota hai?' — jawab kya hoga?
items.a: Foreign key DB level par invariant enforce karta hai, isliye koi bhi path (script, migration, manual fix, doosri service) se aayi galat row reject ho jaati hai. ORM validation sirf app ke through jaane wale writes par chalti hai.
items.x: DB constraint = last line of defence.

items.q: Project defense: 'Is table par tumne 5 indexes banaye — kis query ke liye kaunsa, aur kaunse index ne tumhe nuksan diya?'
items.a: Har index ko uske reader query se map karo (customer_id, sale_date) → per-customer timeline; phir batao ki write-heavy table par index count ne INSERT latency badhaya, isliye ek redundant index drop kiya aur ek composite index ko do single-column indexes ko replace karne diya.
items.x: Index ka justification uska query hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare dashboard ke numbers galat hain to user ko pata kaise chalega?' — honestly kya bologe?
items.a: Metric definitions versioned hain aur har number ke saath as-of timestamp aur definition tooltip hai; galat number ka detection kai tarah se hota hai: raw table se cross-check query, alert on day-over-day jump, aur definition change ka changelog.

items.q: Project defense: 'Transaction kab use karte ho aur kab nahi — ek example do.'
items.a: Transaction tab jab ek business action multiple rows/tables ko atomically badalta ho: order + order_items + inventory decrement. Nahi use karte jab single-statement write ho (wo khud atomic hai) — transaction sirf lock hold time badhata hai.
items.x: Atomicity chahiye to transaction, warna nahi.

items.q: Project defense: 'Agar traffic 10x ho jaaye to SQL layer me pehla kya tootega?'
items.a: Sabse pehle write path par lock contention aur connection pool exhaustion. Plan: read replicas for reporting, write ko queue/batch me convert, hot counters ko pre-aggregate karo, aur connection pooling limits tune karo. Aur batao ki 10x par kya measure karoge (p95, pool wait time, deadlocks).

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare migration rollback plan kya hai?'
items.a: Forward-only migrations with a tested down-path: har migration ke saath data-safe rollback (nullable add → backfill → constraint), pre-migration backup, aur feature flag se app-side switch off karna. Claim nahi — runbook me exact commands hain.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne SQL injection ke liye kya kiya, aur proof kya hai?'
items.a: Saare queries parameterized hain (no string concatenation), ORM/query builder ke placeholders use hote hain, aur ek test hai jo malicious input (' OR 1=1 --) bhejta hai aur verify karta hai ki woh data ban ke rehta hai, query nahi.

items.q: Project defense: 'Normalization vs denormalization — tumhare project me kahan kaunsi choose ki aur kyun?'
items.a: OLTP tables 3NF me hain (customers, orders, order_items) taki update anomalies na hon; reporting/analytics ke liye ek denormalized summary table hai jo nightly refresh hoti hai. Reason: write correctness vs read speed ka trade-off.
items.x: Ek hi jawab nahi, context hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare system me ek user ne galat data dekh liya kyunki replica lag tha — kaise rokoge?'
items.a: Write ke response me version/timestamp bhejo; agar user ka read us version se peeche hai to primary se serve karo (read-your-writes), ya write ke baad short window me us user ke reads primary par pin karo. Aur accept karo ki post-write immediate reads eventually-consistent path se nahi guzarne chahiye.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare paas 3 candidates hain — CTE, temp table aur materialized view — ek reporting query ke liye kaunsa chunoge aur kyun?'
items.a: Day-fresh summary chahiye to materialized view (refresh schedule ke saath), ek query ke andar multi-step logic hai to CTE, aur kai queries same intermediate ko reuse karti hain to temp table. Decision data volume, freshness requirement aur reuse par depend karta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare expense tracker me category aggregate slow kyun nahi hai — proof?'
items.a: Expenses table par (category, spent_on) composite index hai aur report ka date filter sargable range me hai, isliye EXPLAIN me index range scan dikhta hai, seq scan nahi. Numbers bata sakta hoon: 200k rows par p95 30ms.

items.q: Project defense: 'Null-safe logic kahan-kahan miss hui thi aur usse kaunsa bug aaya?'
items.a: Ek anti-join ('customer ne order nahi kiya') NULL rows ko galti se include kar raha tha, isliye count galat aaya. Fix: WHERE s.id IS NULL (NULL ko condition me true nahi banne dena) aur ek test jo NULL-heavy fixture par dono cases verify karta hai.
items.x: NULL bug ko test se band karo.

items.q: Project defense: 'Interviewer tumse poochta hai tumne jo upsert likha usme race kaise handle ki' — exact jawab?
items.a: UNIQUE constraint (user_id, date) par INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE — database hi serialize karta hai, isliye do concurrent requests me se ek insert aur ek update me convert ho jaati hai. App-level 'pehle select karo' wala check race-proof nahi tha.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhara data retention plan kya hai — delete ya archive?'
items.a: Hot data 12 months database me, usse purana archive table me move (INSERT ... SELECT → verify counts → DELETE in batches), aur GDPR-type delete requests ke liye hard-delete path jo sab tables me user_id se chalta hai. Batches se lock time control me rehta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne SQL me testing kaise ki — unit tests hain ya manual?'
items.a: Schema + seed data ek fixture se aate hain, aur queries ko tests se cover kiya (duplicate detection, anti-join, pagination boundaries, NULL cases) — test in-memory SQLite par chalta hai aur expected rows assert karta hai. Manual verification sirf EXPLAIN/plan ke liye.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare project ka sabse bada data risk kya tha aur kaise band kiya?'
items.a: Honest jawab: reporting query OLTP database par chalti thi aur peak par latencies bump karti thi. Mitigation: read replica + nightly summary table + statement timeout, aur dashboard me 'as of' timestamp taaki stale data claim na kare.

items.q: 'Find customers whose order total dropped month over month' — iska approach interview me kaise explain karoge?
items.a: Pehle month-wise aggregates banao, phir LAG se pichhla month laao aur decrease wale rows filter karo: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) mo, SUM(amount) amt FROM sales GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT customer_id, mo, amt, LAG(amt) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY mo) AS prev FROM m WHERE amt < LAG(amt) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY mo);

items.q: students me 10 rows aur sales me 25 order rows hain. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students st LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.student_id = st.id; kya dega?
items.a: 25 se zyada ya barabar (har matching order row ek output row deti hai, aur bina order wale student ke liye ek NULL row) — exactly 25 nahi, kyunki kai students ke multiple orders hain. Unique students gine to COUNT(DISTINCT st.id).
items.x: LEFT JOIN ke baad grain left table ka nahi rehta.

items.q: Real-world: 'pichhle quarter ke repeat buyers' report chahiye — definition aur query dono do.
items.a: Definition: woh customers jinhone pichhle quarter me 2 ya zyada distinct months me order kiya. WITH q AS (SELECT customer_id, strftime('%Y-%m', sale_date) AS mo FROM sales WHERE sale_date >= :q_start AND sale_date < :q_end GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS active_months FROM q GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
items.x: Repeat buyer ka definition hi metric hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumne kaunsa index kyun chuna aur kaunsa deliberately nahi banaya?'
items.a: Chuna: (customer_id, sale_date) composite index, kyunki reader query per-customer timeline hai aur ye prefix + range dono serve karta hai. Nahi banaya: low-selectivity status column par index, kyunki planner seq scan chunta aur write cost bina fayde badhta.
items.x: Dono justify karo: chuna aur chhoda.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhare project me query performance ka budget kya hai aur usse enforce kaise karte ho?'
items.a: Budget: read p95 < 50ms, write p95 < 100ms, ek request me at most 8 queries. Enforcement: test me query count assert, slow-query log par alert, aur CI me critical queries ka EXPLAIN check.
items.x: Budget likha ho to enforce ho sakta hai.

items.q: Project defense: 'Tumhara sabse bada table 5 saal me kitna badega aur uspar plan kya hai?'
items.a: Estimate: rows/day x 365 x 5, phir size = rows x average row width. Plan: date-based partitioning, purana data archive table me (batched move), aur summary tables taaki dashboard bade table ko touch na kare.

items.q: Project defense: 'Ek incident me dashboard par galat number aaya — root cause kya tha aur permanently kya badla?'
items.a: Root cause: metric query refunded orders ko bhi count kar rahi thi (status filter missing). Fix: filter add, metric definition docs me lock, ek regression test jo known fixture par expected count assert karta hai, aur dashboard par 'as of' timestamp.

items.q: Checkpoint: WHERE vs HAVING ko ek line me explain karo (bina example ke).
items.a: WHERE rows par GROUP BY se pehle filter karta hai; HAVING aggregate result par group level par filter karta hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: INNER, LEFT aur anti-join ke output ka farq teen points me likho.
items.a: INNER: sirf match hui rows. LEFT: left ki saari rows + NULL bhara right. Anti-join (LEFT + IS NULL): left ki woh rows jinka koi match nahi.

items.q: Checkpoint: NULL ke saath kaam karte waqt teen rules likho.
items.a: 1) = NULL kabhi true nahi, IS NULL use karo. 2) COUNT(col) NULL skip karta hai, COUNT(*) nahi. 3) NOT IN (… NULL …) khaali result deta hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: GROUP BY ke baad SELECT me kaunse expressions allowed hain?
items.a: Sirf grouping keys aur aggregates (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX ya aggregate-wrapped expressions). Baaki columns ka koi single meaningful value nahi hota.
items.x: Group ke andar kya 'ek' hota hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: ROW_NUMBER / RANK / DENSE_RANK ke output ko tie example (values 10,10,8) par likho.
items.a: ORDER BY value DESC: ROW_NUMBER → 1,2,3; RANK → 1,1,3; DENSE_RANK → 1,1,2.

items.q: Checkpoint: index kab use nahi hoga — teen common wajah likho.
items.a: Column par function/expression lagana, leading wildcard LIKE '%x', aur low-selectivity column (planner seq scan sasta samajhta hai).

items.q: Checkpoint: ACID ke chaaron letters aur ek-ek line ka matlab likho.
items.a: Atomicity: sab ya kuch nahi. Consistency: constraints maintained. Isolation: concurrent transactions alag dikhein. Durability: commit ke baad crash-proof.

items.q: Checkpoint: transaction ke andar kaunse kaam nahi karne chahiye — teen likho.
items.a: 1) User input ka wait (HTTP call, sleep) — locks hold rahenge. 2) Bade batch operations ek hi transaction me. 3) DDL + long data migration ek saath (kai engines me DDL autocommit hota hai).

items.q: Checkpoint: duplicate rows dhoondhne ka standard SQL pattern likho.
items.a: SELECT key, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY key HAVING COUNT(*) > 1; — aur delete se pehle ROW_NUMBER wali subquery me dry run karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: pagination ka safe pattern kya hai?
items.a: ORDER BY mein unique tie-breaker (id) rakho aur aage badhne ke liye keyset (WHERE (ts, id) < last_seen) use karo — OFFSET bade page par mehnga hota hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: slow query debug ke chaar step likho.
items.a: 1) EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) se plan. 2) Estimated vs actual rows compare. 3) Sargability/index check. 4) Rewrite/partition/pre-aggregate, phir dobara measure.

items.q: Checkpoint: foreign key aur index me kya rishta hai (aur ek common misunderstanding)?
items.a: Foreign key constraint + index alag cheezein hain: FK integrity enforce karta hai, par kai engines child column par index automatically nahi banate — bina index wala FK join ko slow kar deta hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: CTE ka structure aur uska ek plus ek minus likho.
items.a: WITH name AS (SELECT ...) SELECT ... FROM name; Plus: readability + reuse. Minus: kai engines me optimization barrier ban sakta hai, isliye bade case me temp table/join se compare karo.

items.q: Checkpoint: LEFT JOIN ke baad WHERE vs ON me filter ka farq ek line me likho.
items.a: Filter ON me → LEFT behaviour intact (non-matching rows NULL ke saath aate hain). Filter WHERE me → NULL rows drop, join practically INNER ban jaata hai.
items.x: Filter ki jagah behaviour badalti hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: parameterized queries kyun mandatory hain?
items.a: Injection rokne ke liye (values query text nahi bante) aur query plan reuse ke liye — performance aur security dono ka fayda.

items.q: Checkpoint: 3NF ka short rule likho.
items.a: Har non-key column sirf key par depend kare — non-key se non-key dependency (transitive) nahi honi chahiye.

items.q: Checkpoint: COUNT(*) vs COUNT(col) vs COUNT(DISTINCT col) — ek-ek line.
items.a: COUNT(*) = saari rows. COUNT(col) = non-NULL values. COUNT(DISTINCT col) = unique non-NULL values.

items.q: Checkpoint: window function ka minimum syntax likho.
items.a: fn() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY col [ROWS BETWEEN ...]) — PARTITION optional, ORDER aur frame behaviour decide karte hain.
items.x: OVER ke andar sab decide hota hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: SQL me date filter ka safest pattern kya hai?
items.a: Half-open range: WHERE ts >= :start AND ts < :end — BETWEEN se safer, kyunki time component inclusive boundaries ko tod deta hai.

items.q: Checkpoint: production me DDL change ka safe sequence likho.
items.a: Nullable column add → batched backfill → default + NOT NULL → constraint lagao; har step alag deploy, aur pehle rollback plan likho.
